subject: biology
title: Nucleic Acids (HL) Adventure 3: Translation and the genetic code
welcome_lead: Today you'll translate a codon stream at HL detail — initiation, elongation, termination.
meta_desc: Biology HL — translation, ribosome A/P/E sites, tRNA, peptidyl transferase, initiation/elongation/termination.
final_note: You learned ribosomes have A/P/E sites, peptide bonds form via peptidyl transferase (ribozyme), and the 64-codon code is universal yet degenerate.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Small subunit binds the 5' cap, scans to first AUG.

Initiator tRNA (Met) enters the P site, large subunit joins → 80S ribosome.

In prokaryotes, the Shine-Dalgarno sequence positions the ribosome.

Three sites:
- A site — new aminoacyl-tRNA enters (codon-anticodon match).
- P site — growing peptide attached to its tRNA.
- E site — empty tRNA exits.

Peptidyl transferase (a ribozyme — rRNA, not protein!) catalyses peptide bond formation. Ribosome translocates one codon. Cycle repeats.

Stop codons UAA, UAG, UGA are read by release factors → peptide released → ribosome dissociates.

The code is:
- Universal (same in nearly all life — testament to common ancestry).
- Degenerate (multiple codons per amino acid).
- Unambiguous (each codon → one amino acid).

Polyribosomes (multiple ribosomes per mRNA) maximise output.

What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.
Water moves both directions in the xylem depending on the time of day.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).

mcqs.q: Which direction does water move in the xylem, and what drives it?
options: Water moves up the xylem because roots pump it actively using ATP.
Water moves both directions in the xylem depending on the time of day.
Upwards from roots to leaves — driven mainly by transpiration pull (evaporation at leaves creating tension on the water column).
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.

mcqs.q: What drives water up the xylem in a tall tree?
options: Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Roots actively pump water up to the leaves like a heart.
Transpiration pull — evaporation from leaves creates tension that pulls water up the continuous water column.
